[[Andorra]] sent a delegation to compete at the [[2002 Winter Olympics]] in [[Salt Lake City, Utah|Salt Lake City]], United States from 8–24 February 2002.  This was Andorra's seventh consecutive appearance at a [[Winter Olympic Games]].  The Andorran delegation consisted of three [[alpine skiers]]; [[Victor Gómez (alpine skier)|Victor Gómez]], [[Alex Antor]], and [[Vicky Grau]].  Their best performance in any event was 24th place by Grau in the [[Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Women's slalom|women's slalom]].

==Background==
The [[Andorran Olympic Committee]] was recognized by the [[International Olympic Committee]] on 31 December 1974.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/andorra|title=Andorra – National Olympic Committee (NOC)|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=5 July 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180614194959/https://www.olympic.org/andorra|archive-date=14 June 2018}}</ref>  They first participated in Olympic competition at the [[1976 Winter Olympics]] and have taken part in every [[Summer Olympics|Summer]] and Winter Olympics since.<ref name=SRAND>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/|title=Andorra|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=5 July 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201033705/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/|archive-date=1 December 2017}}</ref>  This was Andorra's seventh consecutive appearance at a Winter Olympics.<ref name="SRAND" /> Andorra had never won a medal in either the Summer or Winter Olympics.<ref name="SRAND" />  The 2002 Winter Olympics were held from 8–24 February 2002; a total of 2,399 athletes took part representing 77 [[National Olympic Committees]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/salt-lake-city-2002|title=Salt Lake City 2002 Winter Games Olympics – results & video highlights|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=11 August 2018}}</ref>  The Andorran delegation to Salt Lake City consisted of three alpine skiers; Victor Gómez, Alex Antor, and Vicky Grau.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/winter/2002/|title=Andorra at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712110525/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/countries/AND/winter/2002/|archive-date=12 July 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Gómez was selected as the flag bearer for the [[2002 Winter Olympics opening ceremony|opening ceremony]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stillmed.olympic.org/AssetsDocs/importednews/documents/en_report_283.pdf|title=List of the 77 delegations in the order they will enter the stadium and the name of their flag bearer|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=24 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170228171609/https://stillmed.olympic.org/AssetsDocs/importednews/documents/en_report_283.pdf|archive-date=28 February 2017|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and for the [[2002 Winter Olympics closing ceremony|closing ceremony]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympic.org/news/flag-bearers-for-the-closing-ceremony-3|title=Flag Bearers for the Closing Ceremony|date=24 February 2002|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161015190109/https://www.olympic.org/news/flag-bearers-for-the-closing-ceremony-3|archive-date=15 October 2016|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

==Alpine skiing==
{{main|Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics}}
[[Victor Gómez (alpine skier)|Victor Gómez]] was 27 years old at the time of the Salt Lake City Olympics, and was a veteran of the [[1992 Winter Olympics|Albertville]], [[1994 Winter Olympics|Lillehammer]], and [[1998 Winter Olympics|Nagano]] Winter Olympics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/go/victor-gomez-1.html|title=Victor Gomez Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180326203041/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/go/victor-gomez-1.html|archive-date=26 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> [[Vicky Grau]] was 26 years old, and had also participated in all three of those Olympics with her compatriot Gómez.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gr/vicky-grau-1.html|title=Vicky Grau Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180327213813/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/gr/vicky-grau-1.html|archive-date=27 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  [[Alex Antor]] was 22 years old, and making his Olympic debut.  He would later represent [[Andorra at the 2006 Winter Olympics|Andorra]] again at the [[2006 Winter Olympics]] in Turin.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/an/alex-antor-1.html|title=Alex Antor Bio, Stats, and Results|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180401213906/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/an/alex-antor-1.html|archive-date=1 April 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

Grau competed in two races, the [[Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Women's slalom|women's slalom]] and the [[Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Women's giant slalom|women's giant slalom]].  First for her, on 20 February, was the slalom. She posted run times of 58.13 seconds<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom-run-1.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Women's Slalom Run 1|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170711150223/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom-run-1.html|archive-date=11 July 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and a faster second run of 57.03 seconds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom-run-2.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Women's Slalom Run 2|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170711150101/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom-run-2.html|archive-date=11 July 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Her combined time was 1 minute and 55.16 seconds, which placed her 24th out of 38 competitors who finished both legs of the race, the gold medal was won by [[Janica Kostelić]] of [[Croatia at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Croatia]] in a time of 1 minute and 46.10 seconds, the silve rmedal was won by [[Laure Pequegnot]] of [[France at the 2002 Winter Olympics|France]], and the bronze by [[Anja Pärson]] of [[Sweden at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Women's Slalom|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=30 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316215016/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-slalom.html|archive-date=16 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Two days later she participated in the giant slalom, finishing her first leg in a time of 1 minute and 21.24 seconds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-giant-slalom-run-1.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Women's Giant Slalom Run 1|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170708040003/http://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-giant-slalom-run-1.html|archive-date=8 July 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  She did not finish the second run, and therefore went unranked for the event; the gold medal was again won by Kostelić, the silver medal by Pärson, and the bronze was taken by [[Sonja Nef]] of [[Switzerland at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Switzerland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-giant-slalom.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Women's Giant Slalom|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316214653/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/womens-giant-slalom.html|archive-date=16 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

On 21 February, both Gómez and Antor took part in the [[Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Men's giant slalom|men's giant slalom]].  Gómez finished the first run in 1 minute and 17.83 seconds<ref name="GSR1">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom-run-1.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Giant Slalom Run 1|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621015911/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom-run-1.html|archive-date=21 June 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and the second in 1 minute and 15.50 seconds.<ref name="GSR2">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom-run-2.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Giant Slalom Run 2|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621020020/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom-run-2.html|archive-date=21 June 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  He finished in 39th place with a time of 2 minutes and 33.33 seconds.<ref name="GSF">{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Giant Slalom|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180316152643/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-giant-slalom.html|archive-date=16 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  Antor was a little faster, he completed his first run in 1 minute and 16.66 seconds<ref name="GSR1" /> and his second in 1 minute and 14.73 seconds.<ref name="GSR2" />  His total time was 2 minutes and 31.39 seconds, which was enough for 36th place, out of 57 classified finishers.<ref name="GSF" />  The gold medal in the giant slalom was won by [[Stephan Eberharter]] of [[Austria at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Austria]] in a time of 2 minutes and 23.28 seconds, the silver medal was won by [[Bode Miller]] of the [[United States at the 2002 Winter Olympics|United States]], and the bronze by [[Lasse Kjus]] of [[Norway at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Norway]].<ref name="GSF" />  On 23 February, Antor participated in the [[Alpine skiing at the 2002 Winter Olympics – Men's slalom|men's slalom]], finishing the first leg in 54.57 seconds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom-run-1.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Slalom Run 1|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323220010/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom-run-1.html|archive-date=23 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>  However, he did not finish the second leg, and was eliminated from the event.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom-run-2.html|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Slalom Run 2|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323155754/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom-run-2.html|archive-date=23 March 2018|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> In the slalom, the gold medal was won by [[Jean-Pierre Vidal]] and the silver by [[Sébastien Amiez]], both [[France at the 2002 Winter Olympics|Frenchmen]], and the bronze was taken by [[Benjamin Raich]] of Austria.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417234701/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/winter/2002/ASK/mens-slalom.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 April 2020|title=Alpine Skiing at the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Games: Men's Slalom|publisher=Sports Reference|access-date=14 August 2018}}</ref>
